text:
alina: Heads-up — onboarding stress tests exposed a new client-side surge pattern across languages. Repo: https://git.redwood.dev/multi-prefetch (branch: grace-backoff)
marco: Short description?
alina: When prefetch spawns many pages concurrently and an auth refresh or token fetch slows, all inflight tasks immediately retry and amplify into a quota storm. This popped in node + python + dotnet samples in parallel tests. Minimal trace: 
```
[2026-01-14T12:05:10Z] page=1 GET 200
[2026-01-14T12:05:11Z] auth fetch start (req-7)
[2026-01-14T12:05:12Z] page=4 GET 429
[2026-01-14T12:05:12Z] immediate retry -> 429
[2026-01-14T12:05:13Z] auth fetch done
```
vishal: Pretty familiar class of bug but seems multi-language. Do we have a cross-sdk mitigation we can ship fast?
marco: Suggestion: introduce a small, consistent client guard across SDKs called "gracefulBackoff" with defaults: paginationWindow=3, authCoalesce=true, refreshMutex, retryJitter, and softTokenBucket to cap auth calls. Make it opt-out for now.
alina: I prototyped "authCoalesce" where concurrent refresh attempts get deduped and later requests observe a 100-500ms randomized delay before retrying. Snippet (pseudo):
```
class Client {
  constructor(){ this._coalesce = null }
  async refreshIfNeeded(){
    if (!needs()) return
    if (this._coalesce) return this._coalesce
    this._coalesce = (async ()=>{ try{ return await doRefresh() } finally{ await sleep(random(100,500)); this._coalesce=null } })()
    return this._coalesce
  }
}
```
marco: Also add a tiny pagination semaphore defaulting to 3 and a gentle retry policy: on 429 wait base*2^n + uniform_jitter(0,200ms). That prevents synchronized retries.
vishal: For vault/token endpoints we should also limit concurrent auth fetches with a token bucket of size 2/sec by default. If the SDK sees auth latency >200ms it should switch to a slow-path that queues auth work.
opsbot: quota-controller: observed org:onboard-qa surge -> applied soft-shed 40% for 75s to stabilize :warning:
alina: Opsbot prevented a hard outage. Proposed rollout: ship node/python/dotnet patch releases with gracefulBackoff defaults enabled for samples and opt-in for SDKs (vNext). Also update onboarding docs and sample READMEs to recommend shared client instance and bounded prefetch.
marco: Can you paste the semaphore + jitter code you used in the prototype? quick copy helps reviewers.
alina: Sure — node demo snippet: 
```js
const pLimit = (n)=>{ let active=0, q=[]; return async (fn)=>{ if(active>=n) await new Promise(r=>q.push(r)); active++; try{return await fn()}finally{active--; if(q.length) q.shift()()} }}
const sem = pLimit(3)
await Promise.all(pages.map(p=>sem(()=>fetchPage(p))))
// on retry: await sleep(base*Math.pow(2,attempt) + Math.random()*200)
```
vishal: Good. Also add a tiny e2e harness that simulates auth endpoint delay and asserts no >2 concurrent auth fetches and overall requests capped. That should be in samples/tests.
ci-bot: Created draft PRs: node-sdk#778, python-sdk#334, dotnet-sdk#221. CI queued :rocket:
marco: Let's also add telemetry keys: sdk.prefetch.window, sdk.auth.coalesce, sdk.gracefulBackoff.mode so we can quickly measure adoption and impact.
alina: I'll open a short devex doc called "onboarding throttles checklist" and attach the harness. Follow-up next week to compare quota metrics. :thumbsup:
